senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being without moral defect or blemish and hence pure
(derivative of Ἀθῆναι ‘Athens,’ 93.393) pertaining to Athens
(derivative of Ἀθῆναι ‘Athens,’ 93.393) a person who lives in or is a native of Athens
(an Aramaic term meaning ‘field of blood’) a piece of land, probably south of the valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, which was bought with Judas money
to separate grain from the husks of plants, either by beating or by being tread on by farm animals
senses.comment: In a number of societies the idea of having animals tread out grain seems to be extremely wasteful and unsanitary, but there is no way of avoiding a translation of such passages in a more or less literal fashion; otherwise, there is no meaning to the context. It may also be important to provide some type of marginal note to explain more clearly what was involved.

senses.def: to direct one’s vision upward
to become able to see, whether for the first time or again
senses.comment: There is nothing in the statement of Luke 7:22 to indicate whether this is a matter of being able to see for the first time or being able to regain one’s lost sight. It is, however, better to assume that it is a matter of regaining sight unless the context specifies ‘being blind from birth’ or ‘always blind.’

senses.def: to cease from an activity in which one is engaged
senses.comment: It is possible that ἀνάπαυσις in Revelation 4:8 should be interpreted as a period of cessation, but such a meaning would only be derivative of this particular context.

senses.def: to become physically refreshed after ceasing activity or work
senses.comment: In the use of ἀναπαύομαι[a] and ἀνάπαυσις[b], the focus of meaning seems to be upon the restorative character of rest rather than mere cessation of activity (see 68.34).

senses.def: (derivative of ἀναπαύομαι[a] ‘to rest,’ 23.80) a location for resting
senses.comment: It is possible, however, to treat ἀνάπαυσις in Matthew 12:43 as not being a place of rest, but simply a state of rest as in ἀνάπαυσις[b] (23.80). Compare Matthew 11:29, in which ἀνάπαυσις appears to refer to a state rather than to a location.

senses.def: relief from trouble and related anxiety
pertaining to fierceness, in the sense of being wild and untamed
to take liquid, normally water, from a container or well
to believe that something is not true
glosses: to not think to be true

senses.def: to refuse to put one’s trust or reliance in something or someone
senses.comment: One of the serious problems involved in rendering ‘to believe’ or ‘to refuse to believe’ is that so frequently the NT text does not indicate precisely the goal or object of such belief.|In a number of languages, however, the syntactic requirements are such that some clear goal must be in the immediate context. For example, in Mark 16:16 it may be possible to translate ‘whoever refuses to believe the good news shall be condemned.’

senses.def: to not believe in the good news about Jesus Christ and hence not become a follower
to fall from a particular point or location

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: that which causes someone to be pleased with something
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
a seaport in Pamphylia
(a possible idiom, literally: mistiness and darkness fall) a serious impairment of sight, possibly involving total blindness
to cause something to become unclean, profane, or ritually unacceptable
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is quite impossible to translate literally the concept of ‘unclean,’ for physical cleanliness and ritual acceptability are completely unrelated. In some languages it is necessary to translate κοινόω[a] or βεβηλόω as ‘to take away its holiness’ or ‘to make something unacceptable to God.’ In many cultures one must express this concept as involving so-called negative taboo.

senses.def: to cause animals to eat, particularly pasturing animals
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret βόσκω in John 21:15 as meaning ‘to tend’ or ‘to take care of,’ especially since βόσκω occurs in a figurative context referring to people. Such an interpretation may be classified in Domain 35 Help, Care For Subdomain D Care For, Take Care Of, as a figurative meaning. However, it seems more likely that βόσκω in John 21:15 should be understood as an instance of figurative usage, and as such it may also be interpreted as βόσκω[b] ‘to take care of,’ 44.1.

senses.def: to herd animals so as to provide them with adequate pasture and to take care of what other needs may be involved
senses.comment: For another interpretation of βόσκω in John 21:15, see βόσκω[a] 23.10.

senses.def: eating by animals
senses.comment: In some languages a distinction is made in terms relating to eating by animals on the basis of the type of food involved, for example, animals which graze on grass in contrast with those who eat refuse, roots, acorns, etc. An additional distinction is sometimes made in the case of animals which are largely meat-eating in contrast with those that are predominantly plant-eating.

senses.def: a military leader and hero of Israel
profound respect and awe for deity
to cause something not to happen
(derivative of διδάσκω ‘to teach,’ 33.224) pertaining to that which is taught
senses.comment: The expression ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις in 1 Corinthians 2:13 is semantically complex. One may interpret this to mean ‘by means of words used in teaching human wisdom’ or ‘by means of words concerning human wisdom as it is taught.’ Though grammatically διδακτοῖς ‘taught’ goes with λόγοις ‘words,’ there is a very close semantic connection between διδακτοῖς and ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας ‘human wisdom.’

senses.def: (derivative of δόγμα[a] ‘law, rule,’ 33.333) to conform to rules and regulations

senses.subdomain: Whom or What Spoken or Written About
senses.def: in the singular, a reflexive reference to a person or thing spoken or written about, and in the plural, a reflexive reference to any and all persons or things involved as subjects of the clause (including first, second and third persons)
a reciprocal reference between entities
to possess certain characteristics, whether inherent or transitory
senses.comment: In some expressions, the verb εἰμί is absent, e.g. μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι ‘truly fortunate are those servants’ Luke 12:37.

senses.def: to be identical with
to exist, in an absolute sense
to occur, of an event
to be in a place
to mark an event as being possible in a highly generic sense
senses.comment: In Hebrews 9:5 one cannot determine precisely those factors which make it impossible for the author to be more precise. It may be simply the urgency of other matters or the limitations of space or even the inappropriateness of such considerations for the topic under consideration. In some languages, however, one must be somewhat more specific, for a strictly literal translation might imply that the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews was simply incapable of producing a detailed analysis. This would, of course, be quite contradictory to the implication of the statement in Hebrews 9:5 and the scope of the wider context.

senses.def: to belong to a particular class
senses.comment: In John 1:1 θεός obviously is a unique member of a class, and therefore syntactically this would appear to be a case of complete identification. One can, however, translate ‘the Word was God’ but not ‘God was the Word.’

senses.def: to correspond to something else in certain significant features
to change from one state to another
(an idiom, literally: to be in the bosom of) to be closely and intimately associated, with the implication of strong affection for
senses.comment: In John 1:18 one may speak of the Son as ‘being at the Father’s side’ or ‘being in closest communion with the Father.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to be in) to continue to perform certain activities with care and concern
senses.comment: The construction in 1 Timothy 4:15, in which ταῦτα μελέτα and ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι appear to be essentially synonymous reinforcements one of the other, would appear to fully justify combining these expressions as essentially equivalent in meaning, but for another interpretation of μελετάω in 1 Timothy 4:15, see 30.20.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to be in death) to be in imminent danger of dying

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to be someone) to be an important person
(an idiom, literally: to be under a yoke) to be in a state of slavery
senses.comment: In 1 Timothy 6:1 ὑπὸ ζυγὸν is redundant in that it simply emphasizes the status of being a slave.

senses.def: a marker of an explanation or a clarification in the same or a different language
senses.comment: In some languages one must make more specific the interpretation of a term in another language. For example, in Mark 3:17 it may be necessary to translate ‘Boanerges, which in another language means Men of Thunder’ or ‘Boanerges, for which we would say, Men of Thunder.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to be in a dwelling, see 7.8) to be alive, with special emphasis upon physical existence on earth
senses.comment: Most languages have rather generic expressions for ‘life’ or ‘to live,’ but sometimes there are idiomatic expressions which may readily fit the types of contexts illustrated by 2 Corinthians 5:6 and 2 Peter 1:13, for example, ‘to have strength,’ ‘to have one’s eyes,’ and ‘to walk about on the earth.’

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a congregation of Christians, implying interacting membership
senses.comment: Though some persons have tried to see in the term ἐκκλησία a more or less literal meaning of ‘called-out ones,’ this type of etymologizing is not warranted either by the meaning of ἐκκλησία in NT times or even by its earlier usage. The term ἐκκλησία was in common usage for several hundred years before the Christian era and was used to refer to an assembly of persons constituted by well-defined membership. In general Greek usage it was normally a socio-political entity based upon citizenship in a city-state (see ἐκκλησία[c], 11.78) and in this sense is parallel to δῆμος (11.78). For the NT, however, it is important to understand the meaning of ἐκκλησία[a] as ‘an assembly of God’s people.’|In the rendering of ἐκκλησία[a] a translator must beware of using a term which refers primarily to a building rather than to a congregation of believers. In many contexts ἐκκλησία[a] may be readily rendered as ‘gathering of believers’ or ‘group of those who trust in Christ.’ Sometimes, as in 1 Corinthians 1:2, it is possible to translate ‘Paul writes to the believers in Christ who live in Corinth.’ Such a translation does, however, omit a significant element in the term ἐκκλησία[a], in that the sense of corporate unity is not specified.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: the totality of congregations of Christians

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a group of citizens assembled for socio-political activities
senses.comment: It is possible that in ἐκκλησία[c] there is somewhat more focus upon the people being together as a legal assembly, while in the case of δῆμος the emphasis is merely upon a meeting of citizens. But in the NT one cannot distinguish clearly between the meanings of these two words.|ἐκκλησία[c] and δῆμος may be rendered in some languages as ‘a meeting of the people who belonged to that place’ or ‘… who were inhabitants of that town’ or ‘… whose homes were in that town.’

senses.def: a relatively small quantity on any dimension

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: pertaining to being of less status than something else

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a living being who is relatively young, often the younger of two objects
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἐμπεριπατέω ‘to walk about among,’ not occurring in the NT) to live or dwell among
to happen, with the implication of there being a particular set of circumstances

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: to be simultaneous with the time of the discourse

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: to occur with high probability at a point of time just subsequent to another point of time
to move out of an enclosed or well-defined two or three-dimensional area
to go out of existence
(an idiom, literally: to come out from the loins, genitals) to be born as the result of the male role in begetting an offspring
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is more satisfactory to speak of the male role in procreation in terms of ‘being the father of’ rather than employing a term which may have undesirable connotations of sexual relations.

senses.def: (idiom, literally: to go in and to go out) to live or to conduct oneself in relationship to some community or group
senses.comment: The semantic focus of these idioms, especially in Acts 1:21 and Acts 9:28, appears to be the manner in which a person conducts himself in relationship to others, but it is possible to imply a certain amount of movement. For example, in Acts 1:21 it is possible to translate ‘during the whole time the Lord Jesus travelled about with us,’ and in Acts 9:28 one could translate ‘Paul stayed with them and went about in Jerusalem.’

senses.def: a marker of cause or reason, often with the implication of a relevant temporal element
to explain the meaning of something, with the implication that the text in question is difficult or complex
senses.comment: In 2 Peter 1:20 ἐπίλυσις clearly involves the interpretation, not the formulation, of a text.

senses.def: to cause someone to experience something, with the implication of imposed authority
a state of being ready for action
pertaining to being devoted to a proper expression of religious beliefs
senses.comment: In a number of languages the concept of ‘living a godly life’ may be best expressed as ‘to live as God would have one live’ or ‘to live like one should who believes in God’ or ‘to always do what God requires.’ In some languages, however, the only equivalent is ‘to live a good life’ or ‘to live always doing good to others.’ The shift from the focus upon religious belief to good living or being good to others results from the fact that in some religious systems there is little or no connection between religious beliefs and moral behavior.

senses.def: a governor in postexilic Jerusalem who was mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus
that which causes or produces death
senses.comment: The phrase ‘deadly poison’ may be rendered as ‘that which can cause death’ or ‘that which causes people to die.’

senses.def: noise or clamor marked by confusion
senses.comment: In some languages it may be legitimate to translate θόρυβος in Acts 21:34 as ‘so much noise from so many people shouting’ or ‘because so many people were shouting different things.’

senses.def: disorderly behavior of people in violent opposition to authority
one who robs temples
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἱερόσυλος in Acts 19:37, see 53.105.

senses.def: one who commits sacrilege by damaging sacred objects in temples
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἱερόσυλος in Acts 19:37, see 57.242.

senses.def: (diminutive of ἰχθύς ‘fish,’ 4.59) any kind of relatively small fish
a marker of concession, with the probable implication of an additional component of contrast
to make fun of or ridicule by laughing at, but evidently also involving verbal communication
to sail down to a coast
(derivative of κατοικέω ‘to dwell,’ 85.69) a place of dwelling, whether an object or area
to be in dangerous circumstances
to expose oneself to danger
an ointment for the eyes
senses.comment: κολλούριον may often be rendered simply as ‘a medicine for the eyes.’

senses.def: any one of several types of flowers, usually uncultivated
senses.comment: Though traditionally κρίνον has been regarded as a type of lily, scholars have suggested several other possible references, including an anemone, a poppy, a gladiolus, and a rather inconspicuous type of daisy.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to kick against the goad) to react against authority in such a way as to cause harm or suffering to oneself
glosses: to hurt oneself by reacting against a person or command

senses.def: a relatively small body of water either natural or artificial, surrounded by land
senses.comment: The use of λίμνη to refer to the Lake of Galilee (also called the Lake of Gennesaret) normally poses no special difficulty, but in the expression ‘lake of fire’ (Revelation 20:10) there are complications, as already noted in 1.22.

senses.subdomain: Regions Below the Surface of the Earth
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: lake of fire (and sulfur), occurring in some slightly different forms six times in Revelation, three times with the addition of θεῖον ‘sulfur’) a place of eternal punishment and destruction
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is impossible to translate literally ‘lake of fire,’ since water and fire seem to be so contradictory that a lake of fire is not even imaginable. It may be possible in some instances to speak of ‘a place that looks like a lake that is on fire,’ but in other languages the closest equivalent may simply be ‘a great expanse of fire.’ In some parts of the world people are fully familiar with the type of boiling magma in the cone of volcanoes, and terms for such a place may be readily adapted in speaking of ‘a lake of fire,’ since volcanic activity would seem to be the basis for this particular biblical expression.

senses.def: (derivative of μαθητεύω[a] ‘to follow, to be a disciple of,’ 36.31) a disciple who is a woman
pertaining to being unusually attractive and beautiful
senses.comment: For μεγαλοπρεπής as part of a title, see 12.6.

senses.def: a title for God, literally: majestic glory
senses.comment: It is rare that one can use a literal rendering of μεγαλοπρεπὴς δόξα as a title for God, since ‘Sublime Glory’ is a quality and not normally a reference to a person or supernatural being.|It is also possible, however, to use a descriptive phrase such as ‘the one who is supremely glorious’ or ‘the one who is glorious above all others’ or ‘God who is supremely glorious.’ See 79.14.

senses.def: to exchange one thing for another
senses.comment: In rendering μεταλλάσσω in Romans 1:25 it is essential to avoid anything which might mean ‘to change something into.’ It is the substitution of one thing for another; hence, ‘exchange’ rather than ‘change’ is the correct gloss.

senses.def: to cease one activity and to start something else in exchange
(derivative of μισθόομαι ‘to hire,’ 57.172) that which has been hired or rented (but in the NT occurring only in reference to a rented dwelling)
senses.comment: In some languages one may speak of ‘rent’ as ‘money paid in order to stay in a place.’ This may be necessary in order to distinguish such payments from a payment made to purchase something.

senses.def: a town in the south central part of Galilee
pasture land in contrast with cultivated fields
senses.comment: ‘Pastures’ are often designated as ‘grass land’ or ‘cattle land.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of νομή[a] ‘pasture,’ 1.98) extension of an area

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: a large piece of cloth, probably of linen λίνον
to be like or similar to something else
to consider something to be like something else
an event involving sudden force and possible violence

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: pertaining to a point near the end of a day (normally after sunset but before night)
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ὀψέ in Mark 11:19 as indicating a period of time, namely ‘evening’ (see 67.197).

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: the period after sunset and before darkness (compare 67.191)

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time subsequent to another point of time, with the implication of relative lateness
pertaining to being located beside the sea or along the shore

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (derivative of ἐπιδημέω ‘to live as a foreigner,’ 85.78) a person who for a period of time lives in a place which is not his normal residence
senses.comment: In Acts 7:6 the expression ‘as strangers in a foreign country’ may be rendered ‘as strangers living in a country which was not their own.’ Similarly, ‘who live as aliens’ may also be rendered as ‘who live in countries not their own’ or ‘who live with people to whose nation they do not belong.’

senses.def: (derivative of πέλεκυς ‘axe,’ not occurring in the NT) to kill by beheading, normally an act of capital punishment
(derivative of περισσεύω[a] ‘to abound,’ 59.52) that which exists in an abundance
to cause something to be wide
(an idiom, literally: to broaden the heart) to make evident that one has affection for someone
pertaining to that which is different in a number of ways

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: pertaining to being stretched out in a position facedown and headfirst
senses.comment: It is also possible that in Acts 1:18 πρηνής could have the meaning of ‘swollen’ or ‘distended,’ a meaning which is linguistically possible, but not widely witnessed to (see apparatus).

senses.def: to move in front of or ahead of, with the implication that both parties are moving in the same direction
to go in front of, in order to show the way
pertaining to what is new and recent, in the sense of not previously existing
to fight with fists, frequently in reference to boxing
senses.comment: This sole occurrence of πυκτεύω in the NT is in a figurative context.

senses.def: the wife of Boaz in the genealogy of Jesus
an alternative form of Σαούλ, 93.327, the Hebrew name of the apostle Paul

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: clothing as a covering
that which constitutes an unwanted spot or stain upon something
to cause someone to be a soldier
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to specify somewhat more clearly the relationship involved in ‘to enlist soldiers.’ For example, the last part of 2 Timothy 2:4 may be rendered as ‘because he must please the one who caused him to be a soldier’ or ‘… who got him to be a soldier’ or ‘… who induced him to be a soldier for him.’ For another interpretation of στρατολογέω in 2 Timothy 2:4, see 55.20.

senses.def: to be a commanding officer of a group of soldiers
senses.comment: For another interpretation of στρατολογέω in 2 Timothy 2:4, see 55.19.

senses.def: to reign as a king together with someone else
senses.comment: Used figuratively in 1 Corinthians 4:8.

senses.def: to seize or snatch by force and to take away with
senses.comment: In a number of languages, one must distinguish carefully between seizure by an animate being and seizure by a force such as the wind.

senses.def: to cause something to be moved off course
glosses: to cause to go off course

senses.def: (derivative of Συρία ‘Syria,’ 93.589) a person who is a native of Syria

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: the quality of humility
senses.comment: The rendering of ταπεινοφροσύνη in Colossians 2:18 as ‘false humility’ is justified in terms of the context, but there is nothing in the word ταπεινοφροσύνη itself which means ‘false.’ It would be possible to render ταπεινοφροσύνη in Colossians 2:18 as ‘subjection to,’ and one might render the entire expression as ‘in abject worship of angels.’ In other languages ‘false humility’ may be rendered as ‘just pretending to be humble’ or ‘appearing to be humble but really being proud.’

senses.def: a reference to the size of something (occurring rarely in an absolute sense)
a degree which is comparable to some other expression of degree
senses.comment: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of this expression in Revelation 16:18 may be ‘that earthquake was indeed very great.’

senses.def: to shake or tremble, often with the implication of fear and/or consternation
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are two distinct terms for trembling, one relating to illness (as in the case of epileptic seizures or the chills and fever associated with malaria) and the other associated with fear.

senses.def: to come near to and to meet, either in a friendly or hostile sense
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is necessary to specify clearly by the choice of terms whether the meeting is friendly or hostile.

senses.def: to have an opinion based on scant evidence, often with the implication of regarding a false opinion as true
Porcius Festus, the successor to Felix as procurator of Palestine; see 93.300
(derivative of φορτίζω ‘to cause to carry a load,’ 15.207) a relatively heavy object which is carried
(derivative of Χανάαν ‘Canaan,’ 93.611) pertaining to Canaan

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning of χρῖσμα ‘to anoint,’ not occurring in the NT) to assign a person to a task, with the implication of supernatural sanctions, blessing, and endowment
senses.comment: It is rare that one can employ a literal rendering of χρίω or χρῖσμα in such contexts as Luke 4:18 and 1 John 2:20, since ‘to pour oil upon someone’ as a means of conveying a supernatural blessing and endowment for a task is culturally very rare. A strictly literal rendering of χρίω or χρῖσμα as ‘to pour oil upon’ is likely to be interpreted either as an insult or as an event preparatory to setting a person on fire and thus to destroy or to torture. Accordingly, in place of a literal rendering of χρίω or χρῖσμα, it is often necessary to employ some such expression as ‘to be appointed by God’ or ‘to be given a special task by God.’

senses.def: pertaining to being beautiful, often with the implication of appropriateness

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: pertaining to a point of time which is particularly appropriate
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret ὡραῖος in Romans 10:15 as implying something which is fine (see 79.10).
